text:
maya: heads-up — p99 latency jumped ~2.3x after the v7-tokenmap rollout to us-west-2 at 03:15. Not a full outage but noticeable tail. Anyone oncall or looking?
raj: saw alerts, digging into traces now. initial look points at longer kv-cache miss chains + bigger attention matmuls on some shards.
ben: interesting, backend metrics show average seq-len up ~12% for the v7 clients (subword density changed). Could be tokenizer producing more subtokens for certain payloads.
zoe: profiling from one affected host: kernel selector flipped to matmul_v2 for batches with >1k total tokens, but matmul_v2 has worse L3/cache usage on this GPU; matmul_fast would have been better. attaching snippet from topdown profiler.
perf-bot: profile id=pf_2026_03_18_0318 // p99=312ms -> 733ms (pre/post). KV cache hit-rate dropped from 91% -> 68% on rollout shard.
maya: attaching the small trace I pulled (paste below). line numbers are coarse.
maya: ```
# tail of request trace (shortened)
request 0x7fc: tokenizer->encode: 1.42ms
kernel_selector: choice=matmul_v2 (reason=seqlen_bucket=long)
kv_cache.lookup: misses=5
matmul_v2: 148ms
postproc: 2.1ms
```
raj: thanks. can we confirm whether the seq-len distribution shift is client-driven (prompt templates) or tokenizer change?
ben: quick diff of tokenizer mapping: v6->v7 added heuristics merging punctuation in a few languages; but for some english contractions it split into extra subtokens. so avg subtokens per word increased on some datasets.
zoe: that explains kv cache churn — more tokens per request -> more cache write/reads -> eviction behavior changes. our batching heuristic uses predicted token-per-request to pick batch size; if that's off we pick bigger batches and push kernel selector into the wrong perf operating point.
onchalant reaction from infra-bot: :deploy: rolled v7-tokenmap to 12/24 hosts in us-west-2 at 03:15
oncall: rolling an emergency rollback to v6 on the affected pool now. ETA ~8m.
maya: can we also short-term mitigate by forcing kernel selector to prefer matmul_fast for those seqlen buckets? Might be config toggle.
zoe: yes, we have a runtime flag kernel_pref.matrix.longseq=matmul_fast for gpus with compute_cap >= 8. I'll push a canary to 2 hosts to validate.
ben: also suggest reducing max_batch_size by 20% for the pool until we get a stable fix — should reduce p99.
raj: I'm running a sim: apply reduced batch size + kernel pref => projected p99 down to ~320ms in sim traces. If rollback completes and sim confirms, let's keep reduced batch until we roll forward a tokenizer patch.
maya: action items: 1) oncall rollback v7->v6 for pool (oncall). 2) zoe push kernel_pref canary (zoe). 3) ben adjust batcher config to -20% (ben). 4) raj run full sim against leftover traffic and confirm p99 (raj). 5) eng-ml to revert tokenizer change or tweak merges (maya -> ping eng-ml).
zoe: pushing kernel_pref canary now, will report results in 2m.
perf-bot: canary telemetry: host h-102 p99 fell 45% after kernel_pref applied. KV hit-rate unchanged (still lower), but matmul latency improved.
ben: batcher tweak is live on one shard; early telemetry looks promising. throughput minor drop ~3% but p99 improves.
oncall: rollback finished at 03:28. pool back to v6. monitoring.
maya: thanks team. keep an eye on any cross-region impact — similar rollout batches were scheduled in eu-west at 03:30, pause them.
raj: paused, also raising follow-up to eng-ml: tokenizer tuning + a regression test that runs seqlen-distribution simulation during tokenmap changes.
zoe: long-term we should make kernel selector fallback smarter: prefer stable kernel if kv-hit-rate drops below threshold. filing ticket.
maya: filing summary for postmortem: short-lived p99 spike due to tokenizer v7 increasing subword density -> kv cache churn + batcher misprediction -> kernel selector flip to suboptimal kernel. Immediate mitigations: rollback + kernel_pref + reduce batch_size. Next steps: tokenizer fix, regression test, kernel selector heuristic improvement, and monitor thresholds.
ben: +1, will add perf graphs to the incident doc.
maya: closing thread but will update incident doc when we have eng-ml plan. :thumbsup:
